title.narrative: Restoring Connectivity and Recovery through Al-Rastan Bridge Rehabilitation

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Al-Rastan Bridge, a critical link on Syria's M5 Highway between Homs and Hama, remains dangerously damaged yet vitally important for regional mobility, commerce, and humanitarian operations. Despite severe structural deterioration to its deck, beams, and support columns, the bridge continues to serve as an essential corridor for civilian movement, agricultural trade, and aid delivery, with over 5,000 vehicles reportedly crossing daily despite safety risks. The bridge's precarious condition creates dangerous bottlenecks along this strategic north-south artery, forcing heavy trucks, humanitarian convoys, and passenger vehicles to take a longer route around Al-Rastan town or Salamiyeh, using dilapidated secondary roads, which adds at least two hours to the trip and an estimated 20% increase in cost, while impeding economic recovery in surrounding communities. This deterioration compounds existing challenges in Homs and Hama governorates, where 65% of secondary roads remain damaged (World Bank report, 2022), and where unreliable transport networks hinder IDP returns, market access for farmers, and timely humanitarian response.ltbrgtUNDP, in line with its Country Programme Document (CPD), prioritizes the restoration of critical infrastructure to ensure equitable access to essential services for crisis-affected and vulnerable populations. Under this allocation, UNDP will conduct emergency rehabilitation of the Al-Rastan Bridge, which will directly address the mentioned interconnected issues by restoring safe load-bearing capacity, reducing accident risks, and reestablishing efficient transport links. The project is expected to benefit over 70,000 people through improved access to markets, services, and employment opportunities while supporting the broader recovery of Syria's critical transport infrastructure.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented in partnership with the White Helmets , combining technical expertise, public-sector assets, and community-driven execution.ltbrgtThe intervention comprises two key components:ltbrgt1. Bridge structural rehabilitation: Reconstructing damaged elements—slabs, deck, beams, and support columns—to restore full load-bearing capacity and long-term safety.ltbrgt2. Traffic infrastructure upgrades: Installing asphalt surfacing, protective fencing, lighting, signage, and lane markings to ensure safe and regulated post-rehabilitation.ltbrgtThe project adopts a hybrid model, with UNDP providing technical oversight and the White Helmets leading on-the-ground execution, procurement, and financial management. This approach integrates context sensitivity, localization, and inclusive recovery, aligning with UNDP’s broader goals of enhancing resilience, reducing aid dependency, and fostering dignified living conditions in Syria.ltbrgtUNDP will be responsible for the overall management of the project, ensuring oversight of programmatic and fiduciary risks through efficient contractual arrangements, technical standards, risk management, due diligence, and administrative support. This will ensure the implementation of the project on time and the maintenance of high-quality standards for activities and deliverables.ltbrgtlt/pgt
